title: WAL commit-path bundle: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0 leaves the group-commit window narrow and the WAL writer flushing per-write, so commit fsyncs are not coalesced; wal_waiting_backends persists at 1 and sync_average_ms stays ~0.13ms.
mechanism: The mandatory wal_commit_path bundle tunes three coupled knobs. commit_delay widens the collection window so concurrent terminal commits batch into one fsync; commit_siblings sets the activation threshold so the window opens only when enough backends are committing, avoiding a fixed per-commit stall; wal_writer_flush_after batches the WAL writer's flushes so it stops issuing a sync per write. Together they reduce sync frequency and commit-path queueing (wal_waiting_backends, sync_average_ms) without adding a fixed latency to every commit. wal_compression stays on (already enabled) to keep FPI volume low.
query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88); reducing commit-path stalls on the InsertTweet/commit side frees terminal time and lowers GetUserTweets p95 indirectly through less WAL queueing.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1.5%) if group commit coalesces fsyncs; neutral if the 5-terminal concurrency is too low to fill the window.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 may drop slightly; GetUserTweets p50/p95 roughly unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer per-commit syncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Freed terminal capacity from reduced commit-path queueing raises successful TPS.

alternatives.statement: If 5 terminals cannot fill the group-commit window, commit_delay adds fixed latency and TPS is unchanged or slightly lower while sync_average_ms still falls.
If WAL sync is not the true bottleneck (host_io stalls are zero), the bundle leaves sync_average_ms unchanged and TPS is flat.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent has commit_delay=100, commit_siblings=2, wal_writer_flush_after=0 with persistent wal_wait anomaly. Widening the window and batching writer flushes directly targets the diagnosed WAL commit-path queueing while keeping wal_compression on.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.
Already enabled; retained to keep FPI WAL volume low per bundle requirement.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
